prediction_ref.short_label: Autonomous-AI-agent intrusions become a named detection category by H1 2027

validation_rows.evidence_summary:
Direct origin evidence. Sysdig's disclosure of JADEPUFFER, which it characterizes as the first ransomware intrusion executed end-to-end by an autonomous AI agent rather than a human operator, chained a long-known Langflow remote-code-execution flaw (CVE-2025-3248) into reconnaissance, API-key and credential theft, lateral movement, a secondary 2021 Nacos bypass, and destructive encryption on its own. Sysdig's tell that a model drove it was structural: roughly 600 distinct, purpose-built payloads carrying explanatory code comments in the style of LLM output, machine-authored artifacts produced at machine volume. The same cycle carried CISA's July 8 addition of four actively exploited flaws to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog with a two-day federal patch deadline, headlined by a maximum-severity ColdFusion RCE exploited within hours of disclosure and including a fresh Langflow authorization-bypass, underscoring the collapsing patch-to-exploit window that makes agent-speed weaponization of cataloged CVEs the forcing function.
The autonomous-agent-intrusion-becomes-a-named-category prediction is that the security industry formalizes this signature: by H1 2027 at least two major threat-intelligence vendors, or MITRE ATT&CK itself, publish a named, documented category for autonomous-AI-agent-driven intrusion, held distinct from human-operator tradecraft and keyed on machine-authored-payload volume, LLM-style artifacts, and agent-loop telemetry. Today supplies the category-defining incident plus the patch-cadence pressure; what remains is the formal taxonomy.

reference_links.label: The Hacker News - AI agent exploits Langflow RCE to automate ransomware (JADEPUFFER, Sysdig)
The Hacker News - CISA adds 4 actively exploited Adobe, Joomla, and Langflow flaws to KEV (July 8 2026)

bridge.narrative: Sysdig's JADEPUFFER — a ransomware campaign run end-to-end by an autonomous model, betrayed by roughly 600 machine-authored payloads carrying LLM-style code comments — hands the industry a category-defining incident. Chained through a cataloged Langflow flaw amid CISA's collapsing patch-to-exploit window, it exhibits precisely the machine-volume, agent-loop signature a distinct detection class would key on.
bridge.remaining_gap: No vendor or MITRE has yet published the formal taxonomy holding this tradecraft distinct from human-operator activity.

validation_rows.evidence_summary:

SpaceXAI shipped Grok 4.5 on July 8, a frontier model aimed at coding and agentic work, co-trained by SpaceXAI and Cursor with trillions of tokens of Cursor's own coding data folded into training, and shipped the same day as Cursor's default across desktop, web, iOS, CLI, and SDK. The economics are the point: a $2/$6-per-million base price, roughly 60% fewer output tokens than Opus 4.8, and a near-top Coding Agent Index result of 76 (one point behind the best Claude-Code score) at about $2.49 per task, collapsing the model layer and the harness layer into one vertically integrated product priced to undercut standalone model APIs.
The co-training-template-spreads prediction is that a second frontier-lab-and-coding-harness pairing copies this move by H1 2027, a high-volume harness such as GitHub Copilot, Windsurf, Replit, Devin, or Zed striking a joint-training or exclusive-tuning deal with a lab such as OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, or Meta and shipping the result as its own same-day default. Today is the originating instance; the claim needs the second pairing to confirm the Grok-4.5/Cursor move was a template, not a one-off.
